questions.q: A box contains coupons labeled $1,2,3$....n. A coupon is picked at random and the number $\mathrm{x}$ is noted. The coupon is put back into the box and a new coupon is picked at random. The new number is $y$. Then the probability that one of the numbers $\mathrm{x}$, y divides the other is (in the options below [r] denotes the largest integer less than or equal to $\mathrm{r}$ )
questions.solution:
Let $x=1$
favourable out comes $(1,1),(1,2) \ldots \ldots(1, n)$ no. of favourable out comes when $x=1$
=\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{1}\right]

$\therefore$ no. of favourable out comes when $x=1$ or $y=1$
=2\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{1}\right]-1

no. of favourable out comes when $x=2$ or $y=2$ but $x \neq 1, y \neq 1$
2\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{2}\right]-1

Similarly
no. of favourable out comes when $x=k$ or $y=k$ but $x, y \notin\{1,2, \ldots . . k-1\}$
2\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{k}}\right]-1

So probability $=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left[\frac{n}{k}\right]-(1+1 \ldots . . n \text { times })}{n^{2}}$
=\frac{2}{\mathrm{n}^{2}} \sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{n}\left[\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{k}}\right]-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The figure below shows pressure variation in two different sound waves in air with time at a given position. Both the figures are drawn to the same scale.
Which of the following statements is true?
options: Wave 1 has lower frequency and smaller amplitude compared to wave 2
Wave 1 has higher frequency and greater amplitude compared to wave 2
Wave 1 has shroter wavelength and greater amplitude compared to wave 2
Wave 1 has shorter wavelength and smaller amplitude compared to wave 2
questions.solution:
Reason (brief):
- The graphs are \(P\) vs \(t\) at a fixed position and same scale.
- Wave 1 shows more oscillations in the same time \(\Rightarrow\) higher frequency than Wave 2.
- In the same medium, wave speed \(v\) is the same, so \(v=f \lambda \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{v}{f}\). Hence higher \(f\) (Wave 1) \(\Rightarrow\) smaller \(\lambda\).
- The peak displacement from the mean (pressure amplitude) is smaller for Wave 1 than for Wave 2. Therefore, Wave 1: shorter wavelength and smaller amplitude \(\rightarrow\) option (4).
